Investors interested in stocks from the Internet - Software sector have probably already heard of Salesforce (CRM) and Autodesk (ADSK). But which of these two stocks presents investors with the better value opportunity right now? Let's take a closer look.

Everyone has their own methods for finding great value opportunities, but our model includes pairing an impressive grade in the Value category of our Style Scores system with a strong Zacks Rank. The Zacks Rank favors stocks with strong earnings estimate revision trends, and our Style Scores highlight companies with specific traits.

Salesforce has a Zacks Rank of #2 (Buy), while Autodesk has a Zacks Rank of #3 (Hold) right now. This system places an emphasis on companies that have seen positive earnings estimate revisions, so investors should feel comfortable knowing that CRM is likely seeing its earnings outlook improve to a greater extent. But this is just one piece of the puzzle for value investors.

Value investors analyze a variety of traditional, tried-and-true metrics to help find companies that they believe are undervalued at their current share price levels.

Our Value category grades stocks based on a number of key metrics, including the tried-and-true P/E ratio, the P/S ratio, earnings yield, and cash flow per share, as well as a variety of other fundamentals that value investors frequently use.

CRM currently has a forward P/E ratio of 13.31, while ADSK has a forward P/E of 21.32. We also note that CRM has a PEG ratio of 0.78. This popular metric is similar to the widely-known P/E ratio, with the difference being that the PEG ratio also takes into account the company's expected earnings growth rate. ADSK currently has a PEG ratio of 1.37.

Another notable valuation metric for CRM is its P/B ratio of 4.77. The P/B is a method of comparing a stock's market value to its book value, which is defined as total assets minus total liabilities. By comparison, ADSK has a P/B of 16.63.

These are just a few of the metrics contributing to CRM's Value grade of B and ADSK's Value grade of C.

CRM sticks out from ADSK in both our Zacks Rank and Style Scores models, so value investors will likely feel that CRM is the better option right now.

Atlassian Sinks 12% as Slower Growth Outlook Overshadows Beat: "Enterprise AI Has Hit an Inflection Point" ©@Angelo Dee from ภาพของSakorn Sukkasemsakorn via Canva
Key Takeaways

Atlassian shares fell 12% today after it guided to about 13.75% revenue growth for fiscal 2027, against 24% last quarter.

Much of that slowdown comes from Atlassian's planned Data Center wind-down, so the selloff looks overdone.

Reports from monday.com and Salesforce will show whether seat-based software is slowing broadly.

The stock traded at 33x forward earnings before the drop, against a five-year average of 81x.

Atlassian (TEAM:NASDAQ) beat Wall Street's earnings estimate for its fiscal first quarter, and its stock still fell 12% today. Investors looked past it to a full-year guide calling for barely half the quarter's growth.

Next up are work-management rival monday.com (MNDY:NASDAQ), reporting early next week, and Salesforce (CRM:NYSE), which pitches AI agents to the same big companies and reports in early December.

The quarter was the easy part

Revenue rose 24% to $1.77 billion in the quarter ended Sept. 30, and adjusted EPS of $1.65 beat the $1.44 consensus. CEO Mike Cannon-Brookes went further: "Enterprise AI has hit an inflection point."

But for the year ending June 2027, Atlassian guides to about 13.75% revenue growth.

Analysts already expected about that pace going in:

Atlassian (TEAM): revenue, actual and consensus estimates, $ billions, fiscal 2024-2028 (years to June) (TIKR)

So I don't expect the estimates to move much.

A slowdown Atlassian chose

Atlassian stopped selling Data Center software to new customers in March, and plans to retire it in March 2029. So Atlassian expects Data Center revenue to fall about 16% for the year, with Cloud up about 26%. I suspect that explains much of the slowdown.

It's not just Atlassian

monday.com was already slowing: it guided to 16% to 17% revenue growth for the September quarter, from 22% in the June quarter. If its 109% net dollar retention holds next week, I'd put Atlassian's slowdown down to its Data Center switch.

Salesforce's Agentforce ARR passed $1.5 billion at July 31, up more than 240%, yet it guides to just 11% to 12% revenue growth this fiscal year. Its December report will show whether AI agents are adding to growth for seat-priced software yet.

title: What Are Microsoft Investors Betting On?
detail:
What Are Microsoft Investors Betting On?
Trefis Team
Fri, November 6, 2026 at 5:20 AM MST 3 min read
MSFT
GOOG
AMZN
AAPL
ORCL
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Image from Pixabay

For questions about this article or underlying research, email help@trefis.com.

Microsoft (MSFT) stock trades at 26.8 times its adjusted earnings over the last twelve months. This profit figure leaves out one-time items and adds back stock-based pay after tax. That is a lot to pay for a single year of profit, and the multiple is about the same, 26.7 times, against the profit analysts expect for fiscal 2027. That forecast may not add back stock-based pay, so it may count profit on a different basis. The stock only looks cheaper against fiscal 2028 profit. So what kind of growth are you paying for at today's price?

Microsoft Investors Are Betting On Sales Growth

The consensus forecast projects Microsoft's revenue rising about 19% in fiscal 2027, to $395 billion. For fiscal 2028, the forecast anticipates sales growth of 20.5% and net income growth of 20.9%. The forecast's net margin is 37.7% in fiscal 2027 and 37.8% in fiscal 2028. This means the profit growth you are betting on comes from more sales, not from wider margins.

Based on the consensus forecast, Microsoft stock trades at 26.7 times fiscal 2027 earnings and 22.1 times fiscal 2028 earnings. Its trailing multiple on adjusted earnings is 26.8 times.

Has Microsoft Delivered Sales Growth Near The Forecast?

For fiscal 2027, Microsoft is close. Revenue grew 18.8% in fiscal Q1 2027, and management guided for growth of 18% to 19% in fiscal Q2. Over the last twelve months, though, revenue grew 17.9%. This means the fiscal 2028 forecast expects faster sales growth than Microsoft has delivered.

That growth is uneven across the business. In fiscal 2026, Microsoft's Intelligent Cloud segment grew 29.7%, while its More Personal Computing segment shrank 1.1%.

Microsoft reported a net margin of 40.3% in fiscal 2026. The consensus forecast has a lower margin in both coming years. The forecast does not specify whether its profit is reported or adjusted, meaning the two margins may not be measured the same way.

Where Could Microsoft Fall Short Of The Forecast?

The likeliest place is data center capacity. On its October 28 call, management said customer demand continues to exceed available supply, and some third-party GPU capacity Microsoft was counting on for fiscal Q2 has moved into the second half of the fiscal year. Management guided for Azure growth of 49% to 50% in fiscal Q2 and said Microsoft needs further efficiency gains across its fleet to reach it. Any further delay would leave Microsoft less to sell and pull the sales forecast down.

DocuSign shares have travelled a volatile road over the past few years, and the current US$78.92 price invites a simple question for you as an investor: Is the business now priced in a way that its earnings genuinely carry the load the market is putting on them?

Over the past 3 years the stock has delivered a gain of 92.6%, which puts real pressure on the question of whether the underlying earnings justify that kind of journey.

Recent moves to fold AI driven agreement and procurement tools into DocuSign's platform, including partnerships with SAP, Salesforce, Slack and GC AI, can shape how investors think about future profitability and the timing of cash generation tied to its contract workflows.

The analysts covering DocuSign have run their own numbers. See what analysts think DocuSign's shares could be worth.

The issue now is whether DocuSign's current share price is adequately backed by the earnings power of the business today.

If you are weighing DocuSign's AI agreement push against what else is out there, a focused stock screen built around 41 AI small caps can be a useful next research step.

Does DocuSign Look Pricey on Earnings?

The P/E ratio works well for DocuSign because earnings are now a core part of how investors frame the story. At the current price, the stock trades on about 44.7x earnings, compared with roughly 30.2x for the broader Software industry and around 50.3x for its closer listed peers.

That premium against the sector, and discount versus peers, screens as overvalued once you stack it against the tailored fair benchmark implied by DocuSign's own growth profile, margins, size and risk. Because the Intelligent Agreement Management push is gaining traction through SAP solution extensions, GC AI integrations and the Suplari acquisition, the market is already baking meaningful optimism into that 44.7x tag relative to what the model would suggest as a more grounded multiple. Paylocity (PCTY) came out with quarterly earnings of $2.09 per share, beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $1.93 per share. This compares to earnings of $1.75 per share a year ago. These figures are adjusted for non-recurring items.

This quarterly report represents an earnings surprise of +8.29%. A quarter ago, it was expected that this provider of cloud-based payroll and human-resources software services would post earnings of $1.54 per share when it actually produced earnings of $1.84, delivering a surprise of +19.48%.

Over the last four quarters, the company has surpassed consensus EPS estimates four times.

Paylocity, which belongs to the Zacks Internet - Software industry, posted revenues of $451.67 million for the quarter ended September 2026, surpassing the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 2.10%. This compares to year-ago revenues of $408.17 million. The company has topped consensus revenue estimates four times over the last four quarters.

The sustainability of the stock's immediate price movement based on the recently-released numbers and future earnings expectations will mostly depend on management's commentary on the earnings call.

Paylocity shares have added about 12.1% since the beginning of the year versus the S&P 500's gain of 12.3%.

What's Next for Paylocity?

While Paylocity has underperformed the market so far this year, the question that comes to investors' minds is: what's next for the stock?

There are no easy answers to this key question, but one reliable measure that can help investors address this is the company's earnings outlook. Not only does this include current consensus earnings expectations for the coming quarter(s), but also how these expectations have changed lately.

Empirical research shows a strong correlation between near-term stock movements and trends in earnings estimate revisions. Investors can track such revisions by themselves or rely on a tried-and-tested rating tool like the Zacks Rank, which has an impressive track record of harnessing the power of earnings estimate revisions.

Ahead of this earnings release, the estimate revisions trend for Paylocity was favorable. While the magnitude and direction of estimate revisions could change following the company's just-released earnings report, the current status translates into a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) for the stock. So, the shares are expected to outperform the market in the near future. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

It will be interesting to see how estimates for the coming quarters and the current fiscal year change in the days ahead. The current consensus EPS estimate is $1.88 on $447.93 million in revenues for the coming quarter and $8.77 on $1.89 billion in revenues for the current fiscal year.

title: Docusign vs. Monday.com: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?

Docusign vs. Monday.com: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
Brendan Coffey, The Motley Fool

MSFT

Trading disclosure

Deciding between an established market leader and a high-growth challenger is a common challenge for investors. Today, we compare whether Docusign Inc. (NASDAQ:DOCU) or Monday.com (NASDAQ:MNDY) is the better long-term choice.

Docusign pioneered the e-signature category and now seeks to automate the entire contract lifecycle for businesses of all sizes. Meanwhile, Monday.com provides a highly customizable work management platform that helps teams streamline complex workflows. Both companies compete for enterprise budget in the software space, though they currently occupy very different stages of business maturity.

The case for Docusign

Docusign provides Intelligent Agreement Management, including its eSignature and contract lifecycle management solutions. The company operates in the broader tech stocks landscape, serving over 1.8 million customers globally through various digital tools. Major strategic technology partners include Microsoft Corp. (NASDAQ:MSFT), Salesforce.com Inc. (NYSE:CRM), SAP SE (NYSE:SAP), ServiceNow Inc. (NYSE:NOW), Workday Inc. (NASDAQ:WDAY), and Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ:GOOG).

According to its latest annual report, filed for the fiscal year ended Jan. 31, 2026, revenue reached $3.2 billion. This represents an 8.2% increase compared with the prior fiscal year, showing steady expansion in its core markets. Net income for the period was $309.1 million, resulting in a net margin of 9.6% for the latest fiscal year.

As of its January 2026 balance sheet, the current ratio is 0.7x and the debt-to-equity ratio is 0.1x, which measure short-term liquidity and total debt levels. Free cash flow for the fiscal year ended Jan. 31, 2026, reached $1.1 billion. Note that stock-based compensation represented roughly 53.4% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

The case for Monday.com

Monday.com offers an AI work platform designed to manage and automate work across CRM, service, and development segments. The platform is currently used by approximately 250,000 customers worldwide who utilize its flexible Work OS to build custom applications. By focusing on a no-code interface, the company targets a wide range of departments that need to consolidate disparate work processes.

According to its latest annual report, filed for the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, revenue reached $1.2 billion. This marked a significant increase of 26.7% compared with the prior fiscal year. Net income for the period was $118.7 million, while the net margin improved to 9.6% as the company scaled its operations.

Salesforce (NYSE:CRM) and ServiceNow (NYSE:NOW) both reported recently and made the same pitch: agentic AI will power their next phase of growth. Investors have pushed back since. ServiceNow fell 27.58% over the past week, and Salesforce slipped 6.17%. The businesses below look stronger than either move suggests.

24/7 Wall St.
Agentforce Lifts Salesforce While One Guide Spooks ServiceNow Holders

Salesforce posted Q2 revenue of $11.345B, up 10.8%. That pace is steady but modest. The AI layer is growing much faster. Combined Agentforce and Data 360 ARR reached nearly $3.9B, up over 210%, and 50% of Agentforce bookings came from customers buying more credits. That tells me customers keep using agents after they go live. Marc Benioff said "We're seeing incredible demand for our AI and data products, with ARR about to cross $4 billion."

ServiceNow grew subscription revenue 21% to $3.988B, which is faster than Salesforce. It also raised its 2026 AI net new ACV target for the second time this year, to $1.7B. Still, non-GAAP EPS of $1.00 came in below the $1.02 estimate, and the Q4 cRPO guide slowed to 18.5%. Management blamed early renewals and public-sector deals that run on customers' own servers. That explanation sounds reasonable, but I want to see it confirmed.
